verification.stopped: ⏸ Join verification is disabled. New requests will not be verified automatically; administrators must review them manually.

rich_text.enabled: 🎨 Rich text output is enabled. /pkg and /use will send rich text messages; older or third-party clients may not display them correctly.
rich_text.disabled: 📄 Rich text output is disabled. /pkg and /use will send plain text messages.

name_spoiler.enabled: 🫥 Name hiding for new members is enabled. Names will use spoiler formatting so advertising names are not shown directly in the group.
name_spoiler.disabled: 👁 Name hiding for new members is disabled. Names will be shown normally.

verification_mode.current:
🔐 Current join verification mode: %[1]s (source: %[2]s).
Usage: /vmode kernel uses the Linux kernel version; /vmode quiz uses a multiple-choice question; /vmode mixed picks either at random; /vmode auto restores the configuration file setting.
verification_mode.kernel_set: 🔐 Join verification now uses the Linux kernel version. Applicants must run uname -r in a terminal and send their current Linux kernel version.
verification_mode.auto_set: 🔐 Restored the configuration file setting. The current join verification mode is %[1]s.
verification_mode.usage: Usage: /vmode kernel|quiz|mixed|auto. Omit the argument to view the current setting.

auto_delete.current_enabled:
🧹 Automatic deletion of lookup results is enabled. The result and original query will be deleted after %[1]d minutes.
Usage: /autodel off disables it; /autodel <minutes> changes the delay.
auto_delete.current_disabled:
Automatic deletion of lookup results is disabled.
Usage: /autodel on enables it; /autodel <minutes> sets the delay and enables it.
auto_delete.disabled: Automatic deletion of lookup results is disabled. Replies and original queries for /pkg, /use, /bug, /news, /wiki, /bbs, /pkgs, /arm, and /armpkgs will be kept.
auto_delete.enabled: 🧹 Automatic deletion of lookup results is enabled. Results and original queries are retained for %[1]d minutes.
auto_delete.set: 🧹 The deletion delay is set to %[1]d minutes for results and original queries.

help.member:
🤖 Available commands:
/pkg <package> — Search Gentoo packages (official tree, gentoo-zh, GURU)
/use <package> — Show package details and USE flags
/arm <package> — Show Gentoo arm64 keyword status

/pkgs <package> — Compare versions across distributions (also available as /distro <package>)
/armpkgs <package> — Compare arm64 support across distributions
/bug <number> — Look up a Gentoo Bugzilla issue
/news [keywords] — Browse or search Gentoo news
/wiki <keywords> — Search Gentoo Wiki and ArchWiki, including Chinese pages
/bbs <keywords> — Search Linux forums, prioritizing Chinese results

/ping — Show bot status and uptime
/stats — Show today's approvals and rejections
/help — Show this list
help.admin:
👮 Administrators (reply to the target message):
/mute [duration] — Mute the user; defaults to 1h, for example /mute 30m
/unmute — Unmute the user
/ban — Ban and remove the user; delete only the replied message
/sb — Ban and remove the user; also delete all messages from that user
/warn — Warn the user; remove them automatically after %[1]d warnings
/clearwarn — Clear warnings

Other administration commands:
/bantime <duration> — Set the ban duration; 0 means permanent, for example 7d, 12h, or 30m
/autodel [on|off|minutes] — Configure automatic deletion of lookup results
/rich — Toggle rich text for /pkg and /use
/spoiler — Toggle name hiding for new members
/vmode <mode> — Set the verification mode: kernel, quiz, mixed, or auto
/bc — Toggle sender-channel blocking; use /bc allow|deny <channel ID> to manage the allowlist
/start or /stop — Enable or disable join verification
help.direct_message_note: The lookup commands above also work in direct messages, with a limit of %[1]d queries per minute. Review and administration commands only work in the group.
